title: Projectile Definition
description: Top-level structure of a projectile type definition (projectiles/*.json). type selects the motion model; currently only ballistic (SoA integration + ray hit detection) exists. external describes exterior ballistics, terminal describes kinetic terminal effects, and warheads lists the world effects executed after a hit. cookoff describes the contribution of a round to cook-off synthesis: cookoff on the projectile root is the propellant contribution of one stored round, while cookoff on a machine_max:blast warhead is that warhead's contribution when sympathetically detonated. Both are calibrated at the 1 m reference radius, default to zero, and inherit nothing from base_* / near_radius.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference path, used for editor intelligent suggestions and validation

type.description: Motion model type. The only current value is 'ballistic': integrated over SoA arrays and hitting targets with ray or convex sweep tests.

tags.description: Ammo tag list used against launcher required_tags / acceptable_tags / forbidden_tags, e.g. machine_max:caliber/7_62mm, machine_max:ammo/ap. Tags are only for compatibility matching and author-side classification, never for display text.

max_lifetime.description: Maximum lifetime in seconds (SI). Multiplied by 20 internally to get ticks; expiry also goes through the destruction path.

bullet_num.description: Number of projectiles per shot (default 1), used for shotgun-like rounds that fire several pellets at once.

drag_factor.description: Air drag coefficient (proportional to velocity squared); 0 = no drag.

caliber.description: Caliber (mm). Converted to a radius (caliber/2000 m) that feeds both the drag cross-section and the ray hit test; for sub-caliber rounds (e.g. an APFSDS penetrator) write the penetrator diameter.

base_velocity.description: Reference velocity (m/s), the base speed of the velocity-damage model.

base_accuracy_mil.description: Base accuracy (mil / milliradian), the 1-sigma dispersion angle, added to the launcher's accuracy multiplier.

ignition_delay.description: Ignition delay (s) measured from launch; 0 = ignites on leaving the barrel.

thrust.description: Thrust phase (single constant-thrust segment applied along the velocity vector). The whole block may be omitted, defaulting to no thrust.

external.description: Exterior ballistics — determines how the projectile flies. All values are SI units.

base_penetration.description: Penetration at reference velocity (mm RHA). Required.

penetration_velocity_coefficient.description: Penetration velocity coefficient: 0 = independent of velocity, about 1.43 = classic de Marre formula.

damage_velocity_coefficient.description: Damage velocity coefficient: 0 = independent of velocity.

block_damage_factor.description: Block damage factor (0~1). When penetrating a block, kinetic energy times this factor is compared against block durability to decide whether the block is actually destroyed; 0 = never destroys blocks.

stable_distance.description: Stable distance (mm): the longest path a warhead keeps oriented flight inside a material; 0 = unlimited stability (e.g. APFSDS long rod).

unstable_pen_factor.description: Retained penetration factor after instability (0~1); effective penetration after tumbling = current penetration times this factor.

damage_type.description: Damage type dealt by this round (DamageType resource key). Determines which type-dispatched behaviors the damage falls into.

terminal.description: Terminal effects — what happens on impact: penetration checks, damage calculation and block destruction.

cookoff.description: Propellant cook-off contribution: one contribution per stored round when it is sympathetically detonated, excluding warheads inside warheads. The whole block may be omitted, defaulting to zero; it inherits nothing from the kinetic terminal fields. Propellant is already spent on launch, so an in-flight round destroyed by damage contributes no propellant cook-off.

base_penetration.description: Normal-detonation penetration at the reference radius (mm). Required.

base_damage.description: Normal-detonation damage per unit frontal area at the reference radius. Required.

base_impulse.description: Normal-detonation impulse per unit frontal area at the reference radius. Required.

near_radius.description: Normal-detonation reference distance (m): the common reference point of the three base_* values and the near-field plateau radius.

max_radius.description: Normal-detonation hard cutoff radius (m), the ray travel endpoint. Required.

cookoff.description: This warhead's contribution when sympathetically detonated. The whole block may be omitted, defaulting to zero; it is evaluated separately from the normal-detonation base_* / near_radius / max_radius on the same object and inherits nothing from them.

anyOf.description: Parameterized blast warhead. Besides the fields above it accepts normal-detonation presentation fields such as front_speed, destroy_blocks, drop_items, causes_fire, particles, particle_scale, damage_type and light.

type.description: Warhead effect type dispatched by registry name, e.g. machine_max:blast.

anyOf.description: Any other world effect type; its fields are defined by that effect's own Codec and are not constrained here.

warheads.description: Warhead effect list — world effects executed in order after hit detection. An empty list means a pure kinetic round (only the direct kinetic hit applies).

rha.description: Perpendicular equivalent thickness used for hit resolution (mm). This is a hard gate: without penetration the default final damage is 0.

durability.description: Structural hit points; the projectile is destroyed once accumulated damage reaches this value.

vulnerability.description: Vulnerability — armor and structural hit points of this round as a target. The whole block may be omitted, meaning the round cannot be destroyed (it holds no kinematic trigger body).

hit_detection.description: Hit detection primitive — how this round finds targets as an attacker. ray = centroid ray (hit threshold is target radius only); sweep = convex sweep of its own radius (threshold = attacker radius + target radius).

type.description: Guidance law type dispatched by registry name, e.g. machine_max:pure_pursuit.

guidance.description: Guidance component — self-contained algorithm parameters and limits. The whole block may be omitted, defaulting to pure ballistic flight; fields are defined by that law's own Codec.

visual.description: Visual properties — tracer (tracer_color / tracer_alpha / tracer_width / tracer_length / tracer_light_*), muzzle flash (muzzle_flash), fire particles (fire_particles), projectile model and texture (model / texture). The whole block may be omitted and falls back to built-in defaults. See ProjectileType.VisualProperties Codec for field details.

sounds.description: Sound properties — fire sounds (fire_sounds), cease-fire tail (cease_fire_sound) and shell sounds (shell_sounds); keys are RPM threshold strings and values are sound events. The whole block may be omitted and falls back to built-in defaults.

penetration.description: Cook-off penetration at the 1 m reference distance (mm), the p term of the synthesis. A zero-damage contribution does not participate in the damage-weighted penetration average.

damage.description: Cook-off damage calibration per unit frontal area at the 1 m reference distance, the d term of the synthesis. Contributions sum linearly into base_damage.

impulse.description: Cook-off impulse calibration per unit frontal area at the 1 m reference distance (N*s/m^2), the j term of the synthesis. Contributions are squared and summed first, then a single square root gives base_impulse.

cookoff.description: One cook-off contribution. All three fields are calibrated at the 1 m reference radius. The object and each field may be omitted, defaulting to zero; explicit negative values, NaN or Infinity are content errors.

examples.description: Machine-gun round — only a propellant cook-off contribution, no warhead
HE shell — the propellant contribution lives on the root object, the warhead's sympathetic-detonation contribution on the machine_max:blast inside warheads
